properties.name: #479 built an in-memory adjacency and wired ONE caller to it — 142 call sites across 20 files still read edges one store prefix scan at a time, including the containment walk inside every region
properties.statement:
FOUND BY ROOT-CAUSING "12.5 s IS STILL TOO LONG" (Anthony, 2026-09-11), AND IT IS NOT ABOUT `design_regions`.

`#479` built `Adjacency` — every edge of the graph indexed both ways, one scan, memoised per write generation — precisely so a traversal reads neighbours from memory instead of the store. Counted today:

    self.outgoing(..) / self.incoming(..) call sites in reflow2-core   142   (20 files)
    call sites that use self.adjacency()                                 1

**The memo serves `impact_neighbors` and nothing else.** `DesignGraph::outgoing` (graph.rs:949) still calls `engine.scan_outgoing_edges` directly, so every detector, rollup and report reads edges one prefix scan at a time — `detect.rs`, `heal.rs`, `hierarchy.rs`, `allocate.rs`, `verify.rs`, `maturity.rs`, `compare.rs` and thirteen more.

⭐ **IT REACHES BACK INTO THE THING #479 WAS FIXING.** `scope_region` = `containment_closure` + `propagate_from`. The second half was memoised; **the first half was not** — `containment_closure` walks CONTAINS edges through `self.outgoing(&id, Some(CONTAINS))`, a store scan per node in the closure, on every one of the 109 region walks.

═══ THE CLASS, WHICH IS THE POINT ═══

This is the same shape as `fact:an-accepted-principle-stopped-at-the-sidecar-it-was-written-for` and as today's dead `unknown field` branch: **a mechanism is built, wired into the one place that motivated it, and the 141 siblings are left as they were.** Nothing in the design or the tests notices, because each individual call site is correct — only the aggregate is wrong.

═══ WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND IT MATTERS BEFORE ANYONE ACTS ═══

⚠️ **ROUTING ALL 142 THROUGH THE MEMO IS NOT OBVIOUSLY RIGHT.** Building the adjacency costs one full scan of ~24,265 edges. A call that reads ONE node's edges would pay that instead of a single prefix scan — a regression for cheap paths, and 142 call sites is a wide blast radius for a change nobody has measured. The memo pays off per write generation, so a read-heavy call wins and a one-shot read loses. **Which call sites are which has not been counted.**

⚠️ AND TWO CANDIDATES WERE MEASURED AND DOWNGRADED ON THE WAY HERE, both mine:
· `published_interfaces()` is scanned once per `propagate_from` and is not memoised — real, but this design holds **22 Interface nodes**, so it is worth a few hundred ms across 109 walks, not seconds. Looked like a lever; is not.
· the discarded ranking (`scope_region` maps `propagate_from`'s result to `node_id` and throws away centrality, path provenance, risk and boundary crossings, and the sort) is structurally wasteful and `PropagateOptions` carries no way to decline it — but the betweenness BUILD is already memoised, so the per-walk remainder is a hashmap lookup and a sort, not the seconds.

🛑 **NO ATTRIBUTION OF THE 12.5 s WAS OBTAINED.** An in-process instrument was written to time the parts and ran four minutes without reaching its first print, on an in-memory graph — which is its own finding about the profile (see below) and is why this node claims a CAUSE OF WASTE and not a share of the seconds.

═══ THE OTHER LEVER, AND IT IS NOT CODE ═══

`tools/reflow2-mcp-launch.sh:26` serves `target/debug/reflow2-mcp`, and no release binary existed on this machine. **Every number in this investigation — the 12.5 s included — is unoptimized**, and `fact:every-cost-number-today-was-a-debug-build…` already measures the profile alone at ~2.2x on this workload. Whether the wrapper should serve a release build is a shipping question nobody has put, and it is free next to touching 142 call sites.
